observation_summary: The compiler incorrectly infers class-level template types when a method defines its own template, leading to type mismatch errors. The fix introduces a filter to restrict inferred template types to those explicitly defined in the current scope.
hypothesis: The TypeInference engine incorrectly infers template types for a class when a method within that class defines its own template. The fix filters the inferred template types to ensure only those relevant to the current scope (the method's template keys) are applied, preventing leakage or incorrect inference of class-level templates.
prediction: The fix in TypeInference.java will show that the inferred template map is being filtered against the set of valid template keys for the current function, confirming that the bug was an over-eager or incorrect inclusion of template types during inference.
experiment_rationale: The provided fix diff clearly shows the addition of a filter (Maps.filterKeys) to the inference process, which is a procedural correction to the template inference algorithm.
reasoning_summary: The bug is a logic error in the type inference algorithm where it fails to correctly scope template type inference. By adding a filter to the inference map, the algorithm is corrected to only consider relevant template keys. This is a classic Algorithm/Method defect as it involves correcting the procedural logic of the inference step.
